newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt seeks bids for BOT container terminal.
newsitem.headline: Egypt seeks bids for BOT container terminal.

text.p: Egypt invited international investors on Monday to bid for a contract to build and run a container terminal under a BOT (build, operate, transfer) system at the southern mouth of the Suez Canal.

The state's General Authority for Red Sea Ports (GARSP) said the terminal would be at Adabiya port in Suez province and the authority would accept bids from January 1 until the first week of March, 1997.

The terminal includes quays 600 metres (2,000 feet) long and 15 metres (49 feet) deep and a storage area of 400,000 square metres (4.3 million square feet), it added. The length of the quays may be extended to 1,000 metres (3,280 feet).
The terminal "enjoys a unique location in Adabiya port and looks at Asia and Africa,"GARSP said.
The preliminary cost is expected to be 200 million pounds ($59 million), the government newspaper al-Ahram said.
Egypt, facing tough competition from other regional traffic routes and declining Suez Canal revenues, is trying to build new free zones in Sinai and around the canal.
Parliament is expected to pass a law creating the Suez free zone during its current session.
